lessons.title: zhǔfu — to exhort; to tell (someone) to be sure to do something
lessons.gloss: to exhort; to tell (someone) to be sure to do something

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Mandarin for to change the name (of), then the Mandarin for to change one's tune.
zhǔfu — "to exhort; to tell (someone) to be sure to do something".
māma zhǔfu wǒ wǎnshang zǎo huí jiā — Mum told me to be sure to come home early tonight.
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

zhǔfu is built from zhǔ 'to entrust' and fu. The first is inherited from Middle Chinese tsyowk (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), glossed 'to entrust to'; the dictionary has no entry for the second, so its history is not settled.
One more word for saying what would happen.

lessons.title: 千万 (qiānwàn) — be sure to (urging); whatever you do
lessons.gloss: be sure to (urging); whatever you do

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Mandarin for to change one's tune, then the Mandarin for to exhort (someone).

blocks.title: You'll want to know: 千万

segments.text: 千万 — qiānwàn — "be sure to (urging); whatever you do".
你一个人在外边千万要保重 nǐ yí ge rén zài wàibian qiānwàn yào bǎozhòng — Out there on your own, be sure to look after yourself.
The new character, in pieces: 万 (wàn) — three strokes: a long bar, a stroke that runs right and turns down with a hook, and a long stroke falling to the left. The next lesson puts it in your hand.

千万 (qiānwàn) is built from 千 'a thousand' and 万 (wàn) 'ten thousand', both inherited from Middle Chinese, tshen and mjonH (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'ten hundreds'; for the second it names a dance and an insect, and the number is not given there. A thousand times, ten thousand times over: the urging sense is usually explained that way.
One more word for saying what would happen.

blocks.title: Script — a bar, a turning hook, a long fall

segments.text: 万 (wàn).
Three strokes, top to bottom.
A long bar across the top.
A turning hook: from under the middle of the bar, a stroke that runs right, turns down and hooks to the left, as in 为 and 月.
A long stroke falling to the left, from the bar down to the lower left.
One, two, three.

segments.instruction: 万 (wàn), all three, with the model in front of you

segments.text: How many strokes in 万 (wàn)? (Three.) Which stroke has the hook? (The second, the turning hook.) Which comes last? (The long fall to the left.)
Source: Hanzi Writer Data 万 (wàn), pinned stroke paths and medians.

lessons.title: 万能 (wànnéng) — able to do everything; all-purpose

blocks.title: You'll want to know: 万能

segments.text: 万能 — wànnéng — "able to do everything; all-purpose".
méiyǒu wànnéng de bànfǎ — There's no way that works for everything.

万能 (wànnéng) is built from 万 (wàn) 'ten thousand' and 能 'able', both inherited from Middle Chinese, mjonH and nong (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the second 'skilled': able in ten thousand things.
One more word for saying what would happen.

lessons.title: suíshí — at any time; whenever needed

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Mandarin for be sure to (urging), then the Mandarin for all-purpose.
suíshí — "at any time; whenever needed".
yàoshi yǒushì nǐ suíshí lái zhǎo wǒ — If anything comes up, come and find me any time.
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

suíshí is built from suí 'to follow' and 时 'the time', both inherited from Middle Chinese, zjwe and dzyi (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'to go along with': whatever the time.
One more word for saying what would happen.

shùnlì — "smooth; without a hitch".
rúguǒ shùnlì dehuà wǒmen wǔ diǎn jiù dào — If all goes well, we'll be there by five.
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

shùnlì is built from shùn 'to go along with' and lì 'favourable', both inherited from Middle Chinese, zywinH and lijH (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'to follow' and the second 'auspicious'.
One more word for saying what would happen.
